sentences.text: The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing No. 83/2017 registered at Police Station Nanak Pura, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Notice.
Mr. Laksh Khanna, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Varun Lal and Investigating Officer (IO) WSI Roshni Sharma and SI Vijay Pal from Police Station Nanak Pura.
4. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no.1 and respondent no. 2 got married on 03.01.2014 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at New Delhi.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.

It is stated that on the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing No. 83/2017 dated 23.10.2019 was registered at Police Station Nanak Pura, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC against the petitioners.

During pendency of the case, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes before the Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi in terms of the Settlement Deed dated 30.09.2019 entered into between the parties, signed by all the Munish Puri & Ors vs State & Anr on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121573601/

sentences.text: 5. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties in terms of the Settlement Deed dated 30.09.2019 entered into between the parties, signed by all the parties and had dissolved their marriage.
6.

It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

7. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 7,00,000/- in two installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 3,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 in the first motion petition.
b. Second installment of Rs. 3,50,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 in the second motion petition.

Today, the parties who are present in Court state that they have settled the matter and respondent No. 2/ complainant states that she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also the fact that the present matter is a family matter, I am of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

10. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 83/2017 registered at Police Station Nanak Pura, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
11. The petition stands disposed of.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
